problems.title: Small time steps do not guarantee loss descent
problems.source_location: Theorem 2, p.4; Algorithm 1, p.5; Proposition 4/Appendix A.2, pp.24–25.
claim: Theorem 2 claims an update improves next-time extrapolated loss when the time decrement is sufficiently small and functions are smooth.
analysis: Choose constant velocity parameters \(\theta=\phi=0.02\), time \(t=0.5\), input \(0.49\), binary logits \((-10000(u-0.5)^2,0)\), and parameter step \(0.001\). The gradient is \(73.105857863\), so \(\theta^+=-0.053105857863\). Old next-time extrapolation remains \(0.49\); the updated extrapolation is \(0.5265529289315-0.073105857863\delta\). For every \(0<\delta\le0.1\), this moves farther from \(0.5\), increasing cross-entropy with clipping inactive. At \(\delta=0.05\), losses are \(1.3132616875\) and \(5.2482877367\). Arbitrarily small time decrements cannot repair an uncontrolled finite parameter step.
result: Theorem2 lacks a parameter-step condition needed for its claimed next-time descent; arbitrarily small time decrements do not repair this smooth finite-step counterexample.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Control the parameter learning rate and gradient alignment through a descent argument, as well as the ODE time discretization.
problems.impact_rationale: An explicit smooth classifier makes the claimed extrapolated-loss descent fail for every sufficiently small time decrement. This directly contradicts the central formal guarantee.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The cutoff construction does not give almost-everywhere strict growth
claim: Proposition 1 requires a nondecreasing Morse-energy flow with strict growth almost everywhere.
analysis: The proof sets an extra cutoff to zero throughout neighborhoods of critical points, not only at the points. Every noncritical initial point in such an open frozen region has constant energy, contradicting almost-everywhere strictness. Nondecrease and existence of some suitable flow are not refuted.
result: The displayed cutoff construction does not establish almost-everywhere strict energy growth. Nondecrease and existence of a different suitable flow are not refuted.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: An existing narrower construction uses \(X=\mu^2\nabla j\), with an interior-positive boundary-defining \(\mu\), avoiding the extra frozen critical neighborhoods. Its scope is a smooth bounded domain with finite-time boundary noncontact, not arbitrary hard-clipped image domains.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
